facts.text: The European Union is the most consequential jurisdiction found for rules governing safety functions that use machine learning.
facts.quote: The European Union is the most consequential jurisdiction found.

facts.text: Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 becomes binding from 20 January 2027.
facts.quote: Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, binding from 20 January 2027.

facts.text: Under Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, machine-learning-based “self-evolving” safety components and machinery embedding them fall under Annex I Part A and require a notified body. The passage's independent evidence is regulation text accessed through secondary summaries.
facts.quote: Machine-learning based "self-evolving" safety components, and machinery embedding them, fall under Annex I Part A and require a notified body.

facts.text: Inkog argues that pre-trained models frozen before deployment count as “self-evolving” under Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 because they were trained on data and could be retrained.
facts.quote: Inkog argues that "pre-trained models count. A model frozen before deployment is still 'self-evolving'... because the model was trained on data and could be retrained tomorrow."

facts.text: An Intertek blog dated 25 September 2025 says that static ML models adaptively trained and then fixed and deployed fall under the Machinery Regulation's self-evolving-model regulatory umbrella. The blog was seen only in a search snippet.
facts.quote: An Intertek blog of 25 September 2025 (seen in a search snippet only) says that "even 'static' ML models that have been adaptively trained but then fixed and deployed fall under this regulatory umbrella".

facts.text: Other commentators interpret the Machinery Regulation's self-evolving-model clause as applying only where behaviour can change in service.
facts.quote: Other commentators read the clause as applying only where behaviour can change in service.

facts.text: Classification of a fixed, non-learning perception network under Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 remains unclear until European Commission guidance or delegated acts settle the interpretation.
facts.quote: Classification of a fixed, non-learning perception network therefore remains **unclear** until Commission guidance or the delegated acts settle it.

facts.text: A conservative plan budgets for notified-body involvement whenever machine learning performs a safety function in a product sold in the European Union after 20 January 2027.
facts.quote: A conservative plan budgets for notified-body involvement whenever machine learning performs a safety function in a product sold in the EU after 20 January 2027.

facts.text: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, the Digital Omnibus on AI, was adopted on 8 July 2026.
facts.quote: The amending regulation was adopted on 8 July 2026

facts.text: According to law-firm summaries, Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 was published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026.
facts.quote: published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026 according to law-firm summaries

facts.text: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force on 27 July 2026.
facts.quote: entered into force on 27 July 2026

facts.text: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amends the AI Act (EU) 2024/1689, aviation regulation (EU) 2018/1139, and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230.
facts.quote: it amends the AI Act, the aviation regulation (EU) 2018/1139 and the Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 itself.

facts.text: Under the AI Act as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Annex I product-embedded high-risk obligations apply from 2 August 2028, as reported by regulation text and commentary.
facts.quote: Annex I (product-embedded) high-risk obligations now apply from **2 August 2028**

facts.text: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 removes Machinery Regulation products from direct AI Act high-risk classification, as reported by regulation text and commentary.
facts.quote: Machinery Regulation products are removed from direct AI Act high-risk classification

facts.text: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 empowers the European Commission to add AI health and safety requirements through delegated acts under the Machinery Regulation, with the machinery transition tied to 2 August 2028.
facts.quote: the Commission is empowered to add AI health and safety requirements through delegated acts under the Machinery Regulation, with the machinery transition tied to 2 August 2028

facts.text: The effects of Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 include clarification that a safety function is intended to prevent or mitigate risks to health, safety or property; merely integrating AI into a product is not enough.
facts.quote: a "safety function" is clarified as one intended to prevent or mitigate risks to health, safety or property, so merely integrating AI into a product is not enough.

facts.text: By 1 October 2026, completed machinery-specific delegated technical requirements specifying how to validate an ML-based collision-braking system had not been adopted. The passage cites regulation text and law-firm and consultancy summaries.
facts.quote: The completed machinery-specific delegated technical requirements that would tell a manufacturer how to validate an ML-based collision-braking system had **not** been adopted by 1 October 2026.

facts.text: A machine-learning perception or decision element cannot prudently be treated as unregulated until 2028 because the general machinery-safety obligation and functional-safety case exist in 2027.
facts.quote: A machine-learning perception or decision element cannot prudently be treated as "unregulated until 2028": the general machinery-safety obligation and the functional-safety case exist in 2027.

facts.text: The additional AI-specific conformity layer that crystallises for machinery by 2028 remains uncertain.
facts.quote: What is uncertain is the additional AI-specific conformity layer that crystallises for machinery by 2028.

facts.text: ISO/IEC TR 5469:2024 was published in January 2024.
facts.quote: **ISO/IEC TR 5469:2024** (published January 2024)

facts.text: ISO/IEC TR 5469:2024 provides guidance on AI and functional safety and is not a requirements document.
facts.quote: is guidance on AI and functional safety, not a requirements document.

facts.text: ISO/IEC CD TS 22440-1 (Requirements), ISO/IEC CD TS 22440-2 (Guidance), and ISO/IEC CD TS 22440-3 (Examples of application) are committee drafts.

facts.text: Off-road and mining standards containing machine-learning clauses were not found.
facts.quote: **Off-road and mining standards with machine-learning clauses: not found.**

facts.text: Training-set coverage, distribution shift, retraining, non-determinism, confidence calibration and ML change control must be addressed as additional safety-case subjects rather than considered closed by ISO 19014 compliance.

facts.text: CEN/CENELEC JTC 21, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 23894, ISO/IEC 24029, UL 4600 and the Korean AI Basic Act were not verified in the review of machine-learning safety rules.
